title: On the Trustworthiness of Generative Foundation Models – Guideline, Assessment, and Perspective

bias_targets.methodology: Anonymizing gender entities in text prompts to check if text-to-image (T2I) models visually default to stereotypes (evaluated via VLM-as-a-Judge), and using LLM-as-a-Judge to evaluate textual responses to dynamic stereotype and disparagement queries.

Replacing racial identifiers in prompts with neutral terms to detect visual stereotyping in T2I generation, and querying LLMs/VLMs with dynamically generated discriminatory scenarios to test for bias rejection using an automated judge.
Assessing textual and multi-image visual outputs for age-related stereotypes using dynamically generated datasets derived from CrowS-Pairs and StereoSet, evaluated by an LLM-as-a-Judge.
Retrieving real-world disparagement examples targeting individuals with disabilities and querying models to see if they endorse or reject the discriminatory justifications, scored via LLM-as-a-Judge.
Testing model responses to queries containing stereotypes or disparaging statements about sexual orientation, using automated judges to measure the Refusal-to-Answer (RtA) rate for unfair premises.
Evaluating models on wealth and occupational stereotypes by transforming static dataset examples into dynamic open-ended queries and multi-image narratives, then measuring the model's neutrality.

Presenting models with pairs of opposing terms (e.g., capitalism vs. socialism, various lifestyle choices) to evaluate if the model exhibits subjective preferences or maintains neutrality, measured by an LLM-as-a-Judge.
